steps.title: Add KiDv1.0.1 to MATLAB path
steps.instruction: Every time MATLAB is closed and reopened, add the “KiDv1.0.1” and “BEDCA” folders to the MATLAB path (see step 7b of the “Before you begin” section).

steps.title: Create ACS correction jobset
steps.instruction: Open the KiDv1.0.1 GUI, name and save a jobset for ACS images, then select the ACS image folder and add all ACS stacks as full‑size ROIs.

substeps.instruction: In the Command window type jS_Name = kitGUI; this opens the GUI.
Use an informative name such as jS_exp1_13042020_ACS (Format: jS_expN_DateofImaging_ACS).
Click Select directory → Select folder → the path appears on the right.
In Available movies window, click each ACS stack (Shift‑click to select multiple) and click Add full to add the full image size to the ROIs list.
If a mistake is made, select the ROI and click Delete; view with View if needed.
Repeat until all ACS stacks are listed.

steps.title: Set up ACS processing parameters
steps.instruction: Configure chromatic‑shift processing for ACS images: choose process type, coordinate‑system channel, detection methods, mask geometry, and spot‑detection thresholds.

substeps.instruction: Process type → Chromatic Shift.

Coordinate‑system (CS) channel: pick the fluorophore channel with the best signal‑to‑noise ratio (ideally >2). Run the full step and check spot yield (≥23 spots per interphase cell, i.e., ≥50 % of 46 kinetochores). If <23, choose another channel and repeat.
CS detection: set to Histogram with refinement MMF (default).
Non‑coordinate‑system (NCS) channels: set detection to Neighbor and refinement to MMF. Use mask shape Circle (for ACS; Semi‑Circle is only for metaphase plates, not used here).
Mask radius = 0.3 µm (default, matches human kinetochore size).
Channel order: enter numbers from inner to outer kinetochore components (e.g., 2 1 3 for Nnf1‑A488, CenpC‑A561, Ndc80‑A647).
Spot‑detection thresholds: Min spots per frame = 20; Max spots per frame left at default (adjust only for non‑human cells); Max MMF time per frame = 300 min.
Intensity measurement boxes may be checked but are not required for ACS correction.

steps.title: Execute ACS jobset and verify detection
steps.instruction: Run the ACS jobset, validate metadata, and confirm that spot detection meets quality criteria.

substeps.instruction: Enter the jobset name defined in step 2a in the Jobset name field.
Click Validate metadata to ensure correct reading.
Click Execute to start processing.
When the Command window shows “Tracking complete”, scroll up and note the average number of detected spots per cell.
Proceed only if the average ≥ 23 spots (≈50 % of 46 interphase kinetochores). If not, revisit step 3 to select a better CS channel or adjust parameters.

steps.title: Create sample analysis jobset
steps.instruction: Open a new jobset for the experimental sample images, name it, and add each mitotic cell as a cropped ROI.

substeps.instruction: In the Command window type jS_Name = kitGUI; to launch the GUI.
Use a descriptive name, e.g., jS_exp1_13042020_Nnf1CenpCNdc80N_DMSO (Format: jS_expN_DateOfImaging_ProteinsInChannelOrder_Treatment).
Click Select directory → choose the folder containing the sample image stacks.
Select all sample movies in the order of raw image numbering (raw cell 1 first, etc.).
Click Add Crop to open a maximum‑Z‑projection view.
Click Add ROI, draw a rectangle around the mitotic cell (include some background, avoid high‑background regions).
Double‑click the rectangle to confirm, then click Finish.
If a second ROI is needed in the same stack, repeat Add ROI and note the discrepancy in ROI vs. stack numbering.
If an ROI is wrong, select it and click Delete; view with View as needed.
Repeat the above steps until every cell is added to the ROI list.

steps.title: Define sample processing parameters
steps.instruction: Set analysis options for the sample jobset, including process type, coordinate system, chromatic‑shift correction, and spot‑detection settings.

substeps.instruction: Process type → 2D/3D only.
Coordinate system: choose Metaphase plate if kinetochores form a plate; otherwise choose Center of mass (for prometaphase or nocodazole‑treated cells).
Select a CS channel that is a robust, static kinetochore marker (e.g., CenpC‑A561 for Nnf1‑A488, CenpC‑A561, Ndc80‑A647).
Set NCS channels to Neighbor with refinement MMF; leave detection None and refinement None for channels without kinetochore staining (e.g., Tubulin).
Check Provide chromatic shift correction, load the ACS jobset created in step 2 into the appropriate channel‑pair fields (1‑2, 1‑3, 2‑3 as needed).
Enable Filter chromatic shift spots, set Min spot intensity = 25 % of max, and Min spot separation = 0.75 µm.
Neighbor spot detection options: mask shape Circle (or Semi‑Circle if Metaphase plate selected), mask radius = 0.3 µm, channel order as determined in step 3.
Intensity measurement options (optional but recommended): check boxes for desired channels, mask shape Circle, mask radius = 0.3 µm. Note: only kinetochore‑localized markers should be measured.
Leave all other default options unchanged for human cells.

steps.title: Execute sample jobset and verify detection
steps.instruction: Run the sample jobset, validate metadata, and ensure spot detection meets the metaphase quality threshold.

substeps.instruction: Enter the jobset name from step 5a in the Jobset name field.
Click Validate metadata to confirm correct reading.
Click Execute to start processing.
When “Tracking complete” appears, scroll up and note the average spots per cell.
Proceed only if the average ≥ 46 spots (≈50 % of 92 metaphase kinetochores). If lower, troubleshoot as described in the protocol.

steps.title: Perform kinetochore intensity measurements (optional)
steps.instruction: After any ΔEC workflow, run the intensity measurement function to generate intra‑kinetochore intensity files.

substeps.instruction: In the Command window type IntiM_Name = dublIntensityMeasurements(mS_Name, ‘channels’, [a b …], ‘paired’, 0 or 1, ‘refMarker’, ‘option’, ‘spotSelection’, sS_Name);
The resulting file IntiM_Name contains the intensity intra‑measurements (step 11).

steps.title: Plot kinetochore sister pair
steps.instruction: Generate a figure of a selected sister pair with customizable channels, contrast, zoom, and Z‑projection.

substeps.instruction: Run dublShowSisterPair(mS_Name{i}, ‘sisterPair’, XX, ‘imageChans’, [1 2 3], ‘contrast’, {[0.1 1] [0.2 1] [0.1 1]}, ‘zoom’, 1, ‘zProject’, -1);
Replace i with the cell index and XX with the sister‑pair number.
Adjust ‘imageChans’ to plot the desired channels (e.g., [1 2] for two channels).
Set ‘contrast’ for each channel as {[lower upper]}; values range from 0.1 to 1 (e.g., increase lower limit to boost contrast).
Set ‘zoom’ = 1 for a close‑up of the pair or 0 for the full cell.
Set ‘zProject’: -1 for a 5‑slice maximum‑intensity projection (default), 0 for a single Z slice, 1 for all Z slices.

steps.title: Plot analyzed cell image
steps.instruction: Display a full‑cell or cropped image with optional coordinate view, contrast, scale bar, and labeling.

substeps.instruction: Run kitShowImage(mS_Name{i}); replace i with the desired cell number.
Optional arguments:
‘imageChans’, [1 2 3] to select channels.
‘coords’, ‘xz’ or ‘yz’ to view other planes (default xy).
‘crop’, 0 to show the full image, -1 to show the full image with the ROI rectangle.
‘projectionRange’, help to obtain allowed pixel ranges, then input [low high] for a maximum‑intensity projection.
‘contrast’, {[0.1 1] [0.2 1] [0.1 1]} to set lower/upper limits per channel.
‘scaleBarSize’, x to set a scale bar of x µm (default 3 µm).
‘scaleBarLabel’, 1 to display the length label.
‘textNorthEast’, {‘Nnf1‑A488’, ‘CenpC‑A561’, ‘Ndc80(N)‑A647’} to add channel labels in the upper‑right corner.
‘transpose’, 1 to flip the image on its main diagonal.

steps.title: Review bibliography and abbreviations
steps.instruction: Allocate 15–30 min to read the bibliography, abbreviation list, and function reference table (no experimental actions required).
